text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will announce the agriculture policy at a growers' convention at Islamabad on April 4.
- The government has set up a committee to review taxation issues and suggest measures to simplify them.
- A committee has proposed that the government finance a four-month buffer stock of cotton to meet any emergency.
- Power tariffs are expected to increase to 4.47 rupees per kilowatt per hour by 2002 from the present 2.24.
- President Farooq Leghari has appointed Lieutenant General (Retired) Moinuddin Haider as the new governor of Sindh province.
- The Prime Minister's Adviser on Information and Culture Mushahid Hussain has ruled out the possibility of privatising the national flag carrier, Pakistan International Airlines.
- The United States has urged Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and opposition leader Benazir Bhutto to work together on national issues like rampant political and bureaucratic corruption.
- Senate Chairman Wasim Sajjad said the authority of the upper house could be expanded by allowing it to debate monetary policy, including the national budget.
- Pakistan will observe a unilateral moratorium on the export of anti-personnel land mines, the Foreign Office said.
- Former minister Afzal Khan said President Farooq Leghari did not consult the caretaker cabinet of ex-prime minister Meraj Khalid on the formation of the Council for National Defence and Security.

- Tehrik-i-Insaaf (Justice Movement) chief Imran Khan said his party would launch a protest movement if the government gave any relief to former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's jailed husband Asif Zardari.
